I am a woman farming here in Amhara with my family. This sorghum plot is small, only a tiny piece of my land, and I intercrop it like my mother taught me. I have no schooling and little money, so I must be careful. I will try to put a little DAP if the cooperative brings it in time, and I always spread the manure from my animals because that is what keeps the soil alive. I use my own seed saved from last harvest — the improved seed is hard to get for sorghum and costs too much. I cannot irrigate, I wait for the meher rains. My husband and I and the older children will do the weeding and harvesting ourselves.
